title: Review Event
description: One line of the append-only NDJSON review journal for contract: review-journal/v0. A single finding, verdict, remediation, or gate event emitted by a review seat. Every entry carries its own data classification so a record's sensitivity ceiling is enforceable per the ROE (see docs/standards/fierce-collaboration-review.md).

classification.description: Self-classification of this entry. The cross-enum floor access_tier >= sensitivity is enforced below per the minimum-access-tier-per-sensitivity table in docs/standards/access-tier-classification.md#relationship-to-sensitivity. 'unknown' is valid only as a pair: a half-classified entry (one dimension known, the other unknown) fails closed - classify the other half.

reasoner.description: The reasoner (model) behind an agent, or the literal string 'not-exposed'. The field MUST admit non-exposure: a harness that does not expose its reasoner records 'not-exposed' rather than inventing a value - an invented reasoner is a false provenance record.

anchor.description: Immutable provenance anchor. Labeled digest forms are constrained so a label never claims an algorithm it does not use: 'sha256:<64 hex>' is the digest of one artifact's bytes; 'git-tree:<object-format>:<oid>' is a Git tree object ID covering a reviewed set, with the object format read from the repository (git rev-parse --show-object-format), never assumed - 'git-tree:sha1:<40 hex>' or 'git-tree:sha256:<64 hex>'. Where the branch is subject to rewrite (e.g. squash-before-finalize) or unpushed, prefer a content digest over a commit SHA, since the SHA does not survive the rewrite. A bare commit SHA or a message ID (for a live exchange) is carried as-is.

round.description: Review round. Findings persist across rounds until proven closed. This integer - together with the journal's append order - is the ordering authority; ordering is never derived from sorting finding IDs.

seat.description: The role seat emitting the event. Core seats have contract semantics; x- seats are adopter-specific.

agent.description: The reviewing agent's execution context - the axis panel-variance analysis compares over. participant_ref joins the event to a participant declared in the manifest roster, which is what makes seat/prompt/reasoner variance machine-comparable.

model.description: Deprecated in favor of reasoner; retained for compatibility with earlier v0 emissions.

participant_ref.description: The participant.id declared for this seat in the manifest roster. Strongly recommended on every event; required for variance comparison to be possible.

phase.description: What kind of event this is.

finding_id.description: Stable, seat-namespaced finding identity, reused across rounds and never for a different defect. Recommended shape <SEAT>-<SCOPE>-R<round>-<n> (e.g. SR-PARSE-R1-1); a scope token may itself contain hyphens, because an ID is compared for equality, never parsed. An ID is identity, never ordering: round currency comes from the required integer round field and the journal's append order, not from sorting IDs (R10 sorts lexically before R2, and no zero-padding convention is mandated, precisely so lexical sort is never relied upon). Strongly recommended when phase is finding/verdict/remediation.

target.description: What the event is about - a file:line or an artifact.

severity.description: Finding severity. A P1 is a blocker until green on re-review.

defect_class.description: The defect class this finding belongs to, not only the instance observed (standard section 7). Class identity is what makes convergence checkable: a later instance of a class already found in this review is a remediation-approach failure, not a new finding. Required when phase is finding.

lifecycle.description: Machine-readable finding lifecycle state after this event. A remediation claim is closure-pending, not closed; only the reviewing seat's re-verification moves a finding to closed. deferred requires the deferral object - unlabeled deferral is not closure. Required when phase is finding or verdict.

deferral.description: Required when lifecycle is deferred: a P2/P3 stays non-blocking only with a stated reason the relied-upon claim is unaffected, an owner, and a closure trigger (standard section 7).

evidence.description: The proof carried with the claim. Absence of evidence is not permission to synthesize it.

verdict.description: Reviewer's verified conclusion - not an accepted fix report.

remediation_ref.description: Pointer to the remediation (PR/commit/test) offered by the implementing side.

gate.description: Seat disposition at a gate. An author seat may not record an accepted gate: author-does-not-approve is enforced at the seat level here, and at the person level by the journal-set check joining participant identity.

gate_scope.description: What the disposition covers (standard section 5): dispositions are claim-scoped, so a gate names its review scope, non-goals, and any bounds on the green (e.g. reasoner homogeneity, evidence withheld under the ceiling, environments not exercised). structural marks the ACCEPTED (structural) exception of section 7 and never launders a semantic change.
